label: Late original-phase vowel/a,o,i,n,l,x,c token when the sequence began with p/digit/k/b/h/z
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, never at the delimiter or during copying, and only from step 3 on, mostly t>=4. The rate climbs with orig_idx (about 11% at orig_idx 8) and with being close to <DEL> (to_go 0 holds 45% of mass). The input token has to come from a narrow set: a gives the most (34% of mass), then o, i, n, l, x, c, with w weak. It is much stronger when the first one or two original tokens are p, 2, k, b, 3, 1, h or z. It looks like a graded sum of early-token identity and current token rather than a clean rule: when both orig(0) and orig(1) are in that set, precision is 0.86. The strongest activations are a or o near the end of long sequences that start with p or a digit. It does not fire on digits or other letters as input (apart from rare weak hits), or at t<3. Dev F1 is about 0.51 with mass recall 0.87. Precision is the weak part: plenty of qualifying steps stay below threshold.
